title: Handyman Marketing Agency: How to Choose One That Brings in Real Jobs
html:
A handyman marketing agency is a firm that runs search, ads, website and review work for handyman businesss. The right agency shows its work, explains its reporting and fits your budget and trade. This guide covers what an agency should do and what to ask. It also lists the red flags to watch, so your handyman marketing decision starts with clear questions.

What does a handyman marketing agency do?

A handyman marketing agency should help homeowners with repairs and projects find and choose your company. The services vary, so check which ones the agency runs itself and which it hands to others. The table lists the common services and what to ask about each.

What should you ask a handyman marketing agency before you sign?

Ask questions that show how the agency works and how it reports. Clear answers matter more than a long list of promises.

  • Who does the work? the agency team, a partner or an outside vendor.
  • What will you track? calls, form leads and booked jobs, not only clicks.
  • Who owns the accounts? your ad accounts, site and data should be yours.
  • How do you handle small jobs? how the agency keeps tiny tasks from filling your calendar.

What should a marketing contract include?

A marketing contract should state the scope, the reporting and how you can leave. Vague terms are the most common source of disputes, so read this part first.

  • A written list of services and who does each one.
  • What you will see in reports and how often.
  • Who owns the website, ad accounts and data.
  • How to cancel and what happens to your accounts.

How do you choose a handyman marketing agency?

Choose an agency by testing three things: proof, fit and clarity. Ask each agency for the same information so you can compare them fairly.

  • Proof: examples of work for companies like yours, with the numbers explained.
  • Fit: experience with your trade and your size of company.
  • Clarity: a plain scope, a clear price and reports you can read.

What mistakes should a handyman company avoid when hiring an agency?

The most common mistake is choosing on price or on a promise of fast rankings. A close second is not asking who owns the accounts.

  • Choosing on price alone.
  • Accepting a promise of first page rankings by a set date.
  • Not asking who owns the website and ad accounts.
  • Judging an agency on its first month instead of a full cycle.
  • Skipping a call with an existing client.

What should you see in agency reports?

Agency reports should show a few numbers that explain whether the work is paying off. Ask to see a sample report before you sign.

  • Calls and form leads by channel.
  • Cost per lead and cost per booked job.
  • Rankings and visits for the pages that matter.
  • Reviews gained and ratings over time.
  • What the agency plans to do next and why.

How does an agency fit with the rest of your marketing?

An agency should work with your website, your profile and your team, and not replace them. The best results come when everyone shares the same numbers.

Handyman marketing agency FAQ

A handyman marketing agency helps a handyman business get found and win calls. That usually means local search, paid ads, a website with a quote form and review requests. Ask which of these the agency runs itself, and how it reports calls and booked jobs.

How much does a handyman marketing agency cost?

Prices vary by scope, so ask for a written list of services and a monthly fee. Be wary of any quote with no clear scope or with a cut of your jobs that you did not expect.

Should a handyman hire an agency or do marketing alone?

Doing it alone works at first if you have the time for profiles, reviews and simple ads. An agency helps once marketing takes time from jobs. Choose based on your hours, your budget and how much control you want over the accounts.
